title: Wording and test-robustness LOWs from the WCLI-139 review (none blocking)
description: Follow-ups from the Opus APPROVE at ced8e77 of ward-cli#264 (WCLI-139). (1) errors.ts comment above binding_changed says the checkout "is still registered as far as this refusal knows", which is false on the vanish arm; say the set changed under it, so project_not_registered would mislead. (2) ADR 0022 clause 2 and the unregister.ts comment near the in-transaction check should say "no binding when the command starts" (or "when it was asked"), since project_not_registered is pre-question only. (3) binding_changed sits under the Secrets section comment, which says none of them claims that nothing was changed, while its message says Ward removed nothing: move the entry or amend the comment. (4) test/unregister.test.ts uses profileApprovals.slice(1) in the changed-approval race, which depends on approval order; filter by identity.root instead.

VERDICT: APPROVE

Review of opum-ai/ward-cli#272 (WCLI-143) at 7275f5831aa708074f9dca763f3dd1bd814cce91. I read the diff and the tree at that head. Model: claude-opus-5-5.

Findings (none blocking):

- Item 1 is corrected and true. src/contract/errors.ts:260-264 no longer says the checkout "is still registered". The binding_changed refusal is raised in only one place, src/application/unregister.ts:198-203. It fires when the set is missing (`present === undefined`, the vanish arm), when the project differs, or when the fingerprint differs. "Changed or withdrawn" covers all three. The note that project_not_registered "is for a checkout with no binding when the command started" is also true: that code is thrown only at unregister.ts:148, before the first question.
- Item 2 is corrected and true. The ADR 0022 file, lines 43-44, now reads "no binding at the start … `project_not_registered`; nothing is written". The comment at unregister.ts:193-195 now reads "no binding when the command starts, before any question is asked". Both match line 148.
- Item 3 is corrected by amending the comment (errors.ts:248-253); the entry was not moved. The new claim is true. Nothing is written before the in-transaction check. A throw inside the change callback is wrapped as ChangeFailure inside `db.transaction(...)` before seal or write (src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts:536-548), so the transaction aborts. That backs the message "Ward removed nothing".
- Item 4 is corrected and order-independent. The test "an approval that changes between the question and the write is refused as binding_changed" now filters out approvals whose `root` is `locateCheckout(w.first).root`. In the fixture, the first checkout's approval has that root and the second checkout's approval has a different one. So exactly one approval goes, whatever the order. The test would still fail without binding_changed: the removed approval is in the fingerprint (unregister.ts:115-119). Without the check, runUnregister would resolve, so the `rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "binding_changed" })` assertion fails, and the first checkout's binding count would drop to 0.
- LOW, errors.ts:261-262: "the registration was changed or withdrawn under it" is loose on the approval-only arm. There the binding is untouched and only an approval changed. The next sentence ("The set changed") and the user-facing message ("registration changed") cover this, so it is a wording nit only and needs no action.
- LOW, test/unregister.test.ts (the same changed-approval race test): the after-check `expect(after.profileApprovals).toHaveLength(1)` does not say which root survived. Checking that the survivor is `locateCheckout(w.second).root` would be tighter. Optional.
- Question 3: the ADR change is wording only. "the vault is not written" became "nothing is written", and "with no binding" became "with no binding at the start". No clause was added, removed or reordered, and the decision content is the same. No user-facing error message or hint string changed: every errors.ts and unregister.ts hunk is comment-only, and the binding_changed message (errors.ts:268) is untouched.
- Question 4: the five files touched are .quest/tasks/WCLI-143.json, the ADR 0022 file, src/application/unregister.ts (comment), src/contract/errors.ts (comments) and test/unregister.test.ts. None is a .claude/, CLAUDE.md, settings, workflow or ruleset file, and the test edit is limited to the one race.

Not verified from a tree read:
- The DEC-182 (1) fence path list itself. It is not in this tree (searching for DEC-182 outside .quest/ finds nothing), so I judged question 4 by path class only.
- That bun run check, lore check, lore validate --strict and check-lore-agent-sources pass. I had no shell; for CI I relied on your report that Check, Docs and Tracker integrity are green.
- The writer's claim that the ADR wording was compacted to fit the lore implementation profile's token budget, with max_tokens not raised.
- Whether the .quest record edit was written by the quest CLI rather than by hand. It looks consistent: status moved to In Progress, one implementationNotes entry was added, and updatedAt was bumped.
